mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 3 Series 325d engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 3 Series 325d engine replacement typically costs between £4,500 and £7,500 for a reconditioned six-cylinder unit, depending on the engine code (M57 or N57) and the supplier. Used BMW 3 Series 325d engines: £1,800-£4,000. Reconditioned BMW 3 Series 325d engines: £3,500-£6,500. Rebuilt BMW 3 Series 325d engines: £4,500-£7,500.

mainEntity.name: Does the BMW 325d have timing chain issues?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N57-powered BMW 3 Series 325d (2010-2015) can suffer from timing chain stretch, with the chain mounted at the rear of the engine. Early warning signs include a metallic rattle on cold start. The earlier M57 engine (2006-2010) is less prone to timing chain issues but has its own weaknesses - notably swirl flap failure.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 3 Series 325d?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the age and condition of your car. For an E90 325d worth under £5,000, a timing chain repair or used engine often makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. For an F30 325d worth £8,000+, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine with warranty is a sound investment given the car's retained value.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 3 Series 325d engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 3 Series 325d engine replacement typically takes 12-16 labour hours for the six-cylinder M57 or N57 unit. With a specialist, this usually means 2-4 working days from drop-off to collection. Supply only: engine can be delivered next working day. Supply & fit: allow 3-4 days for the complete job.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 325d and 330d engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both the BMW 325d and 330d use the same 3.0-litre six-cylinder diesel engine family (M57 or N57) - but the 325d is detuned. 325d: 197-204 hp depending on generation. 330d: 231-258 hp depending on generation. The 325d offers nearly all of the 330d's smoothness and torque at a lower purchase price and running cost.

mainEntity.name: What are the common problems with the BMW 325d M57 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M57 engine in the BMW 3 Series 325d (2006-2010) is generally robust, but common issues include: swirl flap failure - flaps can detach and enter cylinders, injector failure, EGR valve clogging, and DPF issues on urban-driven cars.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 3 Series 325d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 325d arrived in 2006 as a six-cylinder diesel positioned between the four-cylinder 320d and the range-topping 330d. Using a detuned version of the 330d's 3.0-litre straight-six, the 325d offered nearly all of the 330d's smoothness and torque at a lower price point. Over its production life, the 325d was powered by two generations of BMW six-cylinder diesel engines - the M57 and the N57 - each delivering effortless refinement and strong real-world performance.

milestones.description: M57D30U2 (197 hp), 2,993 cc, six-cylinder turbo-diesel. Fitted to the E90 325d saloon and E91 325d Touring from launch.
M57D30U2 (197 hp), 2,993 cc. Extended to E92 325d Coupé and E93 325d Convertible.
N57D30 (204 hp), 2,993 cc. Introduced with the E90 LCI (Life Cycle Impulse) update, bringing improved efficiency and reduced emissions.
N57D30 (204 hp), 2,993 cc. Carried over into the F30 325d.
325d badge discontinued in the UK; replaced by the 320d with higher-output B47 engine delivering comparable performance with better fuel economy.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 3 Series 325d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 3 Series 325d is powered by two generations of six-cylinder diesel engines - the M57 and the N57. Both are generally regarded as smooth, refined and durable units. However, they share some common weaknesses: injector failure, swirl flap issues (M57) and timing chain stretch (N57). Rebuilt engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: N57 Timing Chain Stretch - Why the BMW 3 Series 325d N57 Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The N57's timing chain is mounted at the rear of the engine, making it difficult to access and inspect. Chain stretch can lead to catastrophic failure if not addressed. Early warning signs include a metallic rattle on cold start.

repairOptions.longevity: Best if caught early - before chain slip or breakage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When chain has snapped or engine is already damaged

problems.recommendation: If you own an M57-powered BMW 3 Series 325d, have the swirl flaps inspected and consider preventative removal - it's a cheap insurance policy against catastrophic failure. For N57 owners, listen for cold-start rattle and have the timing chain inspected if you hear anything unusual. Both engines are fundamentally robust, but preventative maintenance is key to avoiding a full engine replacement.

problems.h4: M57 Swirl Flap Failure - Why the BMW 3 Series 325d M57 Needs Attention
problems.rootCause: The swirl flaps in the inlet manifold can detach and enter the cylinders, causing catastrophic engine damage. This is a well-documented weakness on the M57 engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove or replace swirl flaps with blanking plates
repairOptions.longevity: Preventative - recommended on all M57 325d models
Only if engine damage has occurred
